speaker: abel_garnish
text: Fifty leaves. I have them. Stand off my light.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: They are clean. The king is at two. You have the morning.

speaker: john_heminges
text: Before we are clever. How many parts, and how many boys?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Twenty-odd, and three.

speaker: abel_garnish
text: Twenty-odd is a number I will hate until the plot names the odd one. Three boys I can see.

speaker: john_heminges
text: The rolls are not out today. The company has not read this.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: They have not read it. This is the book. Let them hear it whole, when you set the day.

speaker: abel_garnish
text: You have a Wife, a Mother, and a Lady in the margin, and I take them for one woman. Shall she have three rolls?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: One: the Lady.

speaker: abel_garnish
text: One woman. One roll. I strike the other two names, and I am not sorry.

speaker: john_heminges
text: Strike them. I will not pay three names for one skirt.

speaker: abel_garnish
text: And here the fellow that carries the Nurse's fan comes on as Kemp. You have set down the player for the part. Shall I head his roll with his own name?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: He'd like it better.

speaker: john_heminges
text: Then head it so. He is not in this room. I will not send for him to admire a name.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The fan is the part. His own name may stand on it. You will not have a new tally out of me.

speaker: abel_garnish
text: 'The two hours' traffic of our stage.' Master Shakespeare, I make it three hours, and it is a lie in the first fourteen lines.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: It's a sonnet, Abel. They're allowed one.

speaker: john_heminges
text: A sonnet I cannot pay. Three hours I can see coming. The lie may stand if this is the book you mean.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: It is the book. The fourteen were last night, for my own mouth. The last line was this morning.

speaker: abel_garnish
text: This morning is a good hour for a last line. I have fifty leaves and a sonnet that will not tell the time.

speaker: john_heminges
text: The Rose has the first Tamburlaine today. You will not cross for it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will not cross. I am Gaunt at two.

speaker: abel_garnish
text: Good. I want the book in my hands, not in a wherry. The Lady, one roll. The fan-carrier under his own name. Twenty-odd, and three. And your lie about the hour.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The Lady. His own name. And the lie. You have them.

speaker: john_heminges
text: I have the count. I have not the rolls. The reading is not this morning.

speaker: abel_garnish
text: I will start the boxes when you have gone to be an old man.

speaker: john_heminges
text: The fee on this book is not today's line. Go and be Gaunt.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Keep the leaves dry. I am not putting anything back into the other play because this one is finished.
